The study included 568 men and 525 women (total N=1093) from seven universities in Tehran, with separate exploratory factor analyses conducted for each gender. The Persian BAS-2 demonstrated a one-factor solution similar to the original English version and showed satisfactory convergent validity and internal consistency, with men scoring significantly higher than women on the measure.

2._section_summary: This discussion section presents findings from a single study examining the psychometric properties of the Persian Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) among Iranian university students. The study found a one-factor structure for the BAS-2 in both men and women, with evidence of convergent validity through correlations with self-esteem and life satisfaction. Notably, the BAS-2 showed a negative correlation with BMI in women (r = -0.24) but a positive correlation in men (r = 0.12), contradicting previous research findings.
